query/feature: sum, avg of int2, int4, int8
example: SELECT grp, sum(i4), avg(i4) FROM t GROUP BY grp

query/feature: sum, avg of float4, float8
example: SELECT grp, sum(f8), avg(f4) FROM t GROUP BY grp
notes: Float sums add in a fixed lane order (same result at any worker count and SIMD level); the last digits can differ from the heap-order sum of the normal plan (relative 1e-9).
query: SELECT grp, sum(f8), avg(f8), sum(f4), avg(f4) FROM cv_types GROUP BY grp

query/feature: sum, avg, min, max of numeric(p<=18, s)
example: SELECT source, sum(total), avg(total) FROM orders GROUP BY 1

query/feature: min, max of integers, dates, timestamps

query/feature: min, max of text, varchar

query/feature: stddev, variance family
example: SELECT source, stddev(total), var_pop(store_id) FROM orders GROUP BY 1
notes: Generic aggregate: PostgreSQL's own transition and final functions run over the scan.

query/feature: corr, covar_*, regr_*
example: SELECT source, corr(total, store_id), regr_slope(total, store_id) FROM orders GROUP BY 1

query/feature: bool_and, bool_or, every, bit_and, bit_or, bit_xor
example: SELECT source, bool_and(deleted_at IS NULL), bit_or(store_id) FROM orders GROUP BY 1
notes: Generic aggregates.
query: SELECT source, bool_and(deleted_at IS NULL), bool_or(total > 400), every(store_id > 0), bit_and(store_id), bit_or(store_id), bit_xor(store_id) FROM orders GROUP BY 1

query/feature: string_agg, array_agg, json_agg, jsonb_agg, json_object_agg
example: SELECT source, array_agg(store_id) FROM orders GROUP BY 1

query/feature: string_agg(x, ',' ORDER BY y), array_agg(x ORDER BY y)
example: SELECT source, string_agg(status, ',' ORDER BY id) FROM orders GROUP BY 1
notes: A tuplesort per group on the order keys, then the transition function.

query/feature: percentile_cont, percentile_disc with a constant fraction
example: SELECT source, percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY total::float8) FROM orders GROUP BY 1
notes: Native kernel: exact histogram of the values, spilled to a tuplesort beyond work_mem. Parallel.

query/feature: percentile_* with an array of fractions, over intervals, text or dates; mode()
example: SELECT store_id % 5 AS g, mode() WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY country_code) FROM orders GROUP BY 1
notes: Generic ordered-set aggregates: one tuplesort per group.
query: @g_ordered_set

query/feature: User-defined aggregates (CREATE AGGREGATE)
condition: transition and final functions not volatile
example: SELECT source, coldiff.sum_sq(total::float8) FROM orders GROUP BY 1
notes: Any immutable or stable aggregate runs as a generic one, on the argument leaves.
query: @g_user_aggregate

query/feature: Aggregate with a volatile transition function or argument
condition: not a function of the data, evaluated per row and per group
example: SELECT source, coldiff.sum_vol(total::float8) FROM orders GROUP BY 1
notes: Same result, normal plan.
query: @g_trap_volatile

query/feature: FILTER (WHERE ...) on any aggregate
example: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'paid'), sum(total) FILTER (WHERE total > 100) FROM orders
query: @f_filter_clause

query/feature: DISTINCT in an aggregate with one varying argument
example: SELECT source, string_agg(DISTINCT status, ',') FROM orders GROUP BY 1
notes: sum, avg, min, max, count, string_agg, array_agg, jsonb_agg (DISTINCT);
query: @g_distinct

example: SELECT source, corr(DISTINCT total, store_id) FROM orders GROUP BY 1
notes: A tuplesort of the argument tuples.
query: SELECT source, corr(DISTINCT total, store_id) FROM orders GROUP BY 1

example: SELECT source, rank('paid') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY status) FROM orders GROUP BY 1

query/feature: Variadic aggregates and aggregates of more than four arguments
example: SELECT source, cv_sum_all(store_id, id % 5, 3) FROM orders GROUP BY 1

query/feature: Aggregates of the columns of a lookup-joined table: count, min, max, sum, avg
example: SELECT o.status, sum(v.weight) FROM orders o LEFT JOIN map_vals v ON v.category = o.source GROUP BY 1
notes: Taken per matching row; int, interval and float4 sums run PostgreSQL's own functions on the distinct values.

query/feature: Generic aggregate (stddev, string_agg(DISTINCT), ...) over a lookup-joined column
example: SELECT s.kind, stddev(s.id) FROM orders o JOIN stores s ON s.id = o.store_id GROUP BY 1
query: SELECT s.kind, stddev(s.id), array_agg(DISTINCT s.country_code ORDER BY s.country_code) FROM orders o JOIN stores s ON s.id = o.store_id GROUP BY 1

query/feature: Aggregate of an expression of leaves: sum(qty * (price - discount))
example: SELECT sum(i.qty * (i.price - i.discount)) FROM orders o, jsonb_to_recordset(o.items) i(qty int, price float8, discount float8)
notes: Up to four leaves per expression, evaluated per element.
query: @g_expr_args

query/feature: Aggregate over a column that is not in the index
condition: the scan reads only indexed columns
example: SELECT status, count(memo) FROM orders GROUP BY 1
notes: Put the column in the index to push it down.
query: SELECT status, count(memo), max(length(memo)) FROM orders GROUP BY 1

query/feature: Aggregates in ROLLUP, CUBE, GROUPING SETS
example: SELECT store_id, status, count(*) FROM orders GROUP BY ROLLUP (store_id, status)
notes: All sets in one scan; GROUPING() and the NULLs of the sets are PostgreSQL's.
query: @t_sets_cube_having

query/feature: Aggregate over a numeric expression PostgreSQL evaluates: division, %, power, sqrt, products past 38 digits, casts, NaN
example: SELECT grp, sum(n2 / 3), max(power(n2, 2)) FROM t GROUP BY grp
notes: A generic aggregate on the argument expression (up to four leaves), evaluated by PostgreSQL per row; the numeric arithmetic is PostgreSQL's own. A kernel aggregate (sum, avg of + - * round) stays exact in 128 bits.
query: SELECT grp, sum(n2 / 3), max(n2 * n2 * n2 * n2), max(power(n2, 2)), max(n2::numeric(8, 1)) FROM cv_types GROUP BY grp

query/feature: min, max, sum, avg of DISTINCT numeric values, percentile_disc and mode() of a numeric column
example: SELECT grp, min(DISTINCT n2), percentile_disc(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY n2) FROM t GROUP BY grp
notes: A generic aggregate over the decoded numeric values; the distinct values and the ordered set go through PostgreSQL's transition and final functions.
query: SELECT grp, min(DISTINCT n2), max(DISTINCT n2), percentile_disc(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY n2) FROM cv_types GROUP BY grp

query/feature: percentile_cont, percentile_disc with a fraction that is a stable expression or a parameter
example: SELECT source, percentile_cont(least(1.0, extract(month FROM now())::float8 / 12.0)) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY total::float8) FROM orders GROUP BY 1
notes: The fraction is evaluated when the scan starts. A fraction that is a column of the group keeps the normal plan (PostgreSQL evaluates it per group and raises its own error outside [0, 1]).
query: SELECT source, percentile_cont(least(1.0, extract(month FROM now())::float8 / 12.0)) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY total::float8), percentile_disc(ARRAY[0.25, 0.75]) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY placed_at) FROM orders GROUP BY source

query/feature: int2, int4, int8 (columns, keys, filters, aggregates)
example: SELECT i2, count(*), sum(i8) FROM t GROUP BY i2
query: SELECT i2, i4 % 3, count(*), sum(i8), avg(i4) FROM cv_types GROUP BY 1, 2

query/feature: float4, float8 (keys, filters, aggregates)
example: SELECT f8, count(*) FROM t GROUP BY f8
notes: A float key is one group per value as float8_eq has it: -0 and 0 together, every NaN together.
query: SELECT f4, f8, count(*) FROM cv_types GROUP BY 1, 2

query/feature: numeric(p, s) with p <= 18
example: SELECT n2, count(*), sum(n2) FROM t GROUP BY n2
notes: Stored as integers scaled by 10^s: keys, predicates, sums, averages, min, max, distinct counts, expressions (+ - *, round, floor, casts to integer) are exact. numeric(p<=15) cast to float8 also feeds sum, avg and percentile_cont.
query: SELECT grp, n2, count(*), sum(n2), sum(n15::float8) FROM cv_types GROUP BY 1, 2

query/feature: numeric(p > 18), unconstrained numeric, negative scale
condition: the index refuses the column, so no query reads it from the index
example: SELECT grp, sum(n38) FROM t GROUP BY grp
notes: The table and the query work as usual; leave the column out of the index.
query: SELECT grp, sum(n38), sum(nfree) FROM cv_types GROUP BY grp

query/feature: CREATE INDEX ... USING sift_col on a numeric(p > 18), char(n), bytea, time, interval, uuid, money, enum, array or range column
condition: 0A000 at CREATE INDEX; leave the column out of the index
example: CREATE INDEX ON t USING sift_col (uuid_col)
notes: The hint lists the types: smallint, integer, bigint, boolean, date, timestamp, timestamptz, numeric(p <= 18, s), real, double precision, text, varchar and jsonb with paths.
query: CREATE INDEX cv_x ON cv_types USING sift_col (u)

query/feature: text, varchar (keys, filters, min/max, distinct; strings of any length)
example: SELECT vc, count(*), min(tx) FROM t GROUP BY vc
notes: A dictionary per segment; strings over 255 bytes are stored inline per unit. Filters on the encoded form.
query: SELECT vc, count(*), min(tx), max(tx) FROM cv_types GROUP BY vc

query/feature: char(n), name
condition: not a leaf type of the column index
example: SELECT ch, count(*) FROM t GROUP BY ch
notes: Cast to text in a view or an expression index to use it. A sift_table reads char(n) keys (T24).
query: SELECT ch, count(*) FROM cv_types GROUP BY ch

query/feature: bytea
condition: not a leaf type of the column index
example: SELECT ba, count(*) FROM t GROUP BY ba
query: SELECT ba, count(*) FROM cv_types GROUP BY ba

query/feature: boolean
example: SELECT b, count(*) FROM t GROUP BY b
query: SELECT b, count(*) FROM cv_types GROUP BY b

query/feature: date, timestamp, timestamptz (keys, filters, min/max, date_trunc of a date)
example: SELECT d, count(*), min(ts), max(tstz) FROM t GROUP BY d
notes: date_trunc of a timestamp or timestamptz as a key: see the group keys.
query: SELECT d, count(*), min(ts), max(tstz) FROM cv_types GROUP BY d

query/feature: time, timetz
condition: not a leaf type of the column index
example: SELECT tm, count(*) FROM t GROUP BY tm
query: SELECT tm, count(*) FROM cv_types GROUP BY tm

query/feature: interval
condition: not a leaf type of the column index
example: SELECT iv, count(*) FROM t GROUP BY iv
notes: An interval built from leaves in an aggregate argument (sum((d2 - d1) * interval)) is evaluated by PostgreSQL.
query: SELECT iv, count(*) FROM cv_types GROUP BY iv

query/feature: uuid
condition: not a leaf type of the column index
example: SELECT u, count(*) FROM t GROUP BY u
query: SELECT u, count(*) FROM cv_types GROUP BY u

query/feature: money
condition: no leaf type for money (an int8 with scale 2: a request to the column engine)
example: SELECT m, count(*) FROM t GROUP BY m
notes: Store it as numeric(18, 2) to push it down.

query/feature: enum
condition: not a leaf type of the column index
example: SELECT e, count(*) FROM t GROUP BY e
notes: Cast to text in an expression index, or keep it as text. A sift_table groups by an enum (T24).
query: SELECT e, count(*) FROM cv_types GROUP BY e

query/feature: arrays (int[], text[]) and ranges
condition: not a leaf type of the column index
example: SELECT ia, count(*) FROM t GROUP BY ia
notes: jsonb arrays of objects are the supported array form (next rows).
query: SELECT ia, count(*) FROM cv_types GROUP BY ia

query/feature: jsonb members declared in the paths option, typed (->>, ->, #>> and casts)
example: SELECT attributes->>'channel', count(*) FROM orders GROUP BY 1
notes: Declare each path with a type: WITH (paths = 'attributes->channel text, metrics.* float8, ...'). A member of another type than declared is stored as an overflow and raises 0A000 where the normal plan casts.
query: SELECT attributes->>'channel', count(*) FROM orders GROUP BY 1

query/feature: jsonb member that is not declared in the paths option
condition: the index does not hold it
example: SELECT attributes->>'device', count(*) FROM orders GROUP BY 1
notes: Add it to paths and REINDEX.
query: SELECT attributes->>'device', count(*) FROM orders GROUP BY 1

query/feature: jsonb array of objects through jsonb_to_recordset, jsonb_array_elements (one level)
example: SELECT i.category, count(*), sum(i.qty) FROM orders o, jsonb_to_recordset(o.items) i(category text, qty int) GROUP BY 1
notes: One lateral unnest per query; elements of one row keep the same-element semantics in filters.
query: SELECT i.category, count(*), sum(i.qty) FROM orders o CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_to_recordset(o.items) AS i(category text, qty int) GROUP BY 1

query/feature: jsonb object with dynamic keys (jsonb_each, jsonb_each_text, metrics ->> 'key')
example: SELECT kv.key, avg((kv.value #>> '{}')::float8) FROM orders o, jsonb_each(o.metrics) kv GROUP BY 1
notes: Declared as key.* type.
query: SELECT kv.key, count(*) FROM orders o CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_each(o.metrics) kv GROUP BY 1

query/feature: jsonb arrays nested deeper than one level, or two arrays unnested together
condition: 0A000 at CREATE INDEX; keep one level of arrays
example: CREATE INDEX ... WITH (paths = 'j.a[]{b[]{c int4}}')
notes: A query with two unnests, or an element compared with another array, keeps the normal plan (see the join rows).
query: CREATE INDEX cv_x ON cv_types USING sift_col (j) WITH (paths = 'j.a[]{b[]{c int4}}')

query/feature: jsonb column with no paths
condition: 22023 at CREATE INDEX; declare the paths
example: CREATE INDEX ON t USING sift_col (j)
query: CREATE INDEX cv_x ON cv_types USING sift_col (j)

query/feature: numeric NaN in an indexed column
condition: 0A000 at query time; SET sift.enable_agg = off for that query
example: SELECT g, sum(n) FROM tbl GROUP BY g
notes: The index stores NaN as NULL with an overflow flag; the scan raises where the normal plan returns NaN. Only the kernels raise; expressions PostgreSQL evaluates (division, functions) rebuild the NaN.
query: -- guc: seq_page_cost = 10000\n-- guc: random_page_cost = 10000\nSELECT g, sum(n) FROM cv_nan GROUP BY g

query/feature: sift_table: scalar columns (integers, floats, text, varchar, date, timestamps, boolean, numeric(p <= 18), char(n), enum)
example: SELECT grp, e, count(*), sum(n2) FROM t GROUP BY grp, e
notes: The engine keeps every type exactly; the aggregate scan reads these.
query: SELECT grp, ch, e, count(*), sum(i4), sum(n2), min(d), max(tx) FROM cv_tt GROUP BY grp, ch, e

query/feature: sift_table: numeric(p > 18) and unconstrained numeric, uuid, interval, bytea, money, time, arrays
condition: stored exactly but not read as values by the aggregate scan
example: SELECT u, count(*) FROM t GROUP BY u
notes: The table, its row scans and indexes work for every type.
query: SELECT bool_and(coverage.plan_of(format('SELECT %s, count(*) FROM cv_tt GROUP BY 1', c)) !~ 'SiftAgg') FROM unnest(ARRAY['n38', 'nfree', 'u', 'iv', 'ba', 'm', 'tm', 'ia']) c

query/feature: GROUP BY a column (dictionary, integer, date, boolean, float, numeric(p<=18))
example: SELECT status, count(*) FROM orders GROUP BY status
notes: Up to 5 group columns; 4 with grouping sets.
query: SELECT store_id, source, status, lang, country_code, count(*) FROM orders GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5

example: SELECT date_trunc('month', placed_at::timestamp)::date, count(*) FROM orders GROUP BY 1
notes: Evaluated by PostgreSQL once per distinct value of the column.

example: SELECT CASE WHEN lang = 'en' THEN source ELSE status END, count(*) FROM orders GROUP BY 1
notes: Evaluated once per distinct tuple of the values, cached across units.

query/feature: GROUP BY date_trunc, extract of a timestamp or timestamptz, or CASE over numeric
example: SELECT date_trunc('month', ts), count(*) FROM t GROUP BY 1

query/feature: float4 / float8 keys
example: SELECT f8, count(*) FROM t GROUP BY f8

query/feature: GROUPING SETS, ROLLUP, CUBE, GROUPING()

condition: PostgreSQL evaluates it per row, the scan once per value
example: GROUP BY random() > 0.5

query/feature: Key over a column that is not in the index
condition: the scan reads only indexed columns
example: SELECT left(memo, 3), count(*) FROM orders GROUP BY 1
query: SELECT left(memo, 3), count(*) FROM orders GROUP BY 1

query/feature: SELECT DISTINCT, DISTINCT ON
condition: not an aggregate; DISTINCT ON picks rows
example: SELECT DISTINCT status FROM orders
notes: Use GROUP BY to get the aggregate scan.
query: @t_distinct_on

query/feature: Key or filter expression over an integer column with a wide range of values (x % 7 of an int8)
example: SELECT i8 % 7, count(*) FROM t GROUP BY 1
notes: Evaluated by PostgreSQL per distinct value that occurs, not per value of the range.
query: SELECT i8 % 7, count(*) FROM cv_types WHERE i8 % 11 <> 3 GROUP BY 1

query/feature: Equality, range, BETWEEN, <> on integers, dates, text, numeric(p<=18)
example: SELECT count(*) FROM orders WHERE store_id BETWEEN 5 AND 50 AND placed_at >= DATE '2024-01-01'
notes: Range tests on the encoded values; zone maps skip whole units on a clustered column.

query/feature: IN and = ANY lists (up to 64 constants for numeric, any length for the others)
example: SELECT count(*) FROM orders WHERE store_id IN (1, 2, 3)
notes: A parameter array or a numeric list over 64 constants: see the next rows.

example: SELECT count(*) FROM t WHERE n2 / (i2 + 1) > 20
notes: Evaluated by PostgreSQL per distinct tuple of values.
query: SELECT count(*) FROM cv_types WHERE n2 / (i2 + 1) > 20 AND n2 > 10.5::float8

query/feature: LIKE, ILIKE, prefix, regex (~), any boolean function of one text or integer column
example: SELECT count(*) FROM orders WHERE source LIKE 'market%'
notes: A lookup table over the distinct values of the column, evaluated by PostgreSQL.
query: SELECT count(*) FROM orders WHERE source LIKE 'market%' OR source ~ '^w' OR source ILIKE '%PLACE%'

query/feature: IS [NOT] NULL, AND, OR, NOT
example: SELECT count(*) FROM orders WHERE status IS NULL OR NOT (store_id < 10 AND lang = 'en')

query/feature: Expressions of leaves: x + y < 20, total * 2 > 300
example: SELECT count(*) FROM orders WHERE store_id + id % 5 < 20
notes: + - * of numeric and float leaves have kernels; the rest is evaluated by PostgreSQL per distinct tuple.

query/feature: Parameters ($1) and stable functions (now(), current_date, a scalar sub-select)
example: SELECT status, count(*) FROM orders WHERE placed_at > current_date - 3000 GROUP BY 1
notes: Custom and generic plans. A qual with no column is a gate evaluated when the scan starts.
query:
-- prepare: (int, text)
-- args: 50, 'paid'
-- guc: plan_cache_mode = force_generic_plan
SELECT status, count(*) FROM orders WHERE store_id < $1 AND status <> $2 GROUP BY 1

query/feature: Volatile function in the WHERE (random(), clock_timestamp())
condition: evaluated per row by PostgreSQL, not a function of the data
example: WHERE store_id < random() * 100
query: @t_volatile_qual

query/feature: Predicate on a column that is not in the index
condition: the scan reads only indexed columns
example: SELECT count(*) FROM orders WHERE length(memo) > 10
query: SELECT count(*) FROM orders WHERE length(memo) > 10

query/feature: Predicate on ctid
condition: not a leaf of the index
example: SELECT grp, count(*) FROM t WHERE ctid >= '(0,1)' GROUP BY grp
notes: The row scan itself supports TID range scans.
query: SELECT grp, count(*) FROM cv_tt WHERE ctid >= '(0,1)' GROUP BY grp

query/feature: EXISTS over an array of objects (same-element semantics), @> containment, jsonb_path_exists / @?
example: SELECT count(*) FROM orders o WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM jsonb_to_recordset(o.items) i(category text, qty int) WHERE i.category = 'Toys' AND i.qty > 2)
notes: Several tests of one element and AND/OR/NOT of tests; also in FILTER.
query: @s7_exists_same_element

query/feature: jsonpath with != or !(), strict mode, variables, a number against a float leaf; @> with null, floats or {}
condition: equality with the heap result is not provable from the index
example: WHERE jsonb_path_exists(items, '$[*] ? (@.kind != "gift")')
query: @t_path_not_equal

query/feature: An element compared with a column of the outer row, a second array in the sub-query, LIMIT or OFFSET in it
condition: the test is no function of the element alone
example: WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM jsonb_to_recordset(o.items) i(qty int) WHERE i.qty = o.store_id % 5)

example: SELECT s.kind, count(*), sum(o.total) FROM orders o JOIN stores s ON s.id = o.store_id GROUP BY s.kind
notes: The joined table is read at executor start with the query's snapshot, hashed by the key, and its columns are keys, filters and aggregate arguments like leaves. Meant for small dimension tables.
query: SELECT s.kind, count(*), sum(o.total) FROM orders o JOIN stores s ON s.id = o.store_id GROUP BY s.kind

query/feature: LEFT JOIN to a small table (unmatched rows give NULLs), filters in ON or WHERE on the joined columns
example: SELECT s.kind, count(o.id) FROM orders o LEFT JOIN stores s ON s.id = o.store_id GROUP BY s.kind
notes: A NULL key matches nothing; text compares as = does (deterministic collations).
query: @j_where_left

query/feature: EXISTS (...) and IN (SELECT ...) (semi join)
example: SELECT count(*) FROM orders o WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM stores s WHERE s.id = o.store_id AND s.kind = 'outlet')
notes: A row stays once however many rows match.
query: @j_semi_exists

query/feature: NOT EXISTS (anti join)
example: SELECT count(*) FROM orders o WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM stores s WHERE s.id = o.store_id AND s.kind = 'outlet')
query: @j_anti_not_exists

query/feature: NOT IN (SELECT ...)
condition: a hashed SubPlan with the NULL rule of NOT IN, no anti join
example: SELECT count(*) FROM orders WHERE store_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM stores WHERE kind = 'outlet')
notes: Write NOT EXISTS to push it down.
query: @t_not_in_subquery

query/feature: RIGHT JOIN, FULL JOIN to a table
condition: the unmatched rows of the table would be output rows with no source row
example: SELECT s.kind, count(o.id) FROM orders o FULL JOIN stores s ON s.id = o.store_id GROUP BY s.kind
notes: Write LEFT JOIN from the side that has the index.
query: SELECT s.kind, count(o.id) FROM orders o FULL JOIN stores s ON s.id = o.store_id GROUP BY s.kind

query/feature: The indexed table on the nullable side of an outer join
condition: the aggregate is over the preserved side
example: SELECT s.kind, count(o.id) FROM stores s LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.store_id = s.id GROUP BY s.kind
query: @t_outer_join_nullable

query/feature: Join to a large table, self join
condition: the joined table is read whole at executor start; fine for dimension tables, wasteful for big ones
example: SELECT count(*) FROM orders a JOIN orders b ON a.customer_id = b.customer_id AND a.id < b.id
notes: Keep the joined table small.
query: SELECT count(*) FROM orders a JOIN orders b ON a.customer_id = b.customer_id AND a.id < b.id

query/feature: Join with no equality of the table's columns (range, ON true), join to a sub-select with GROUP BY or LIMIT, VALUES, a function
condition: nothing to hash the table by, or the right side is a plan and not a table
example: SELECT s.kind, count(*) FROM orders o JOIN stores s ON o.store_id < s.id GROUP BY s.kind
query: SELECT s.kind, count(*) FROM orders o JOIN stores s ON o.store_id < s.id GROUP BY s.kind

query/feature: CTE referenced once, subquery in FROM (pulled up), view
example: WITH x AS (SELECT * FROM orders WHERE store_id < 50) SELECT status, count(*) FROM x GROUP BY status
query: WITH x AS (SELECT * FROM orders WHERE store_id < 50) SELECT status, count(*) FROM x GROUP BY status

query/feature: CTE referenced more than once (several granularities of one series)
condition: planned inline when that plan has a SiftAgg and costs half; not for a CTE with a volatile function
example: WITH base AS (...) SELECT ... FROM base GROUP BY 1 UNION ALL SELECT ... FROM base GROUP BY 2
notes: The arms of one inlined CTE run in one pass over the index.
query: WITH base AS (SELECT o.id AS order_id, o.placed_at, i.qty FROM orders o CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_to_recordset(o.items) AS i(qty int) WHERE o.deleted_at IS NULL) SELECT 'day' AS grain, placed_at AS bucket, count(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders, sum(qty) AS units FROM base GROUP BY 2 UNION ALL SELECT 'month', date_trunc('month', placed_at)::date, count(DISTINCT order_id), sum(qty) FROM base GROUP BY 2

query/feature: UNION ALL of aggregates over the table
example: SELECT 'a', status, count(*) FROM orders GROUP BY status UNION ALL SELECT 'b', lang, count(*) FROM orders GROUP BY lang
notes: Each arm is its own scan unless they share a CTE.
query: SELECT 'a' AS g, status, count(*) FROM orders GROUP BY status UNION ALL SELECT 'b', lang, count(*) FROM orders GROUP BY lang

query/feature: Per-order aggregates (SELECT id, keys, agg ... GROUP BY id, keys) under an outer GROUP BY
condition: the inner per-order GROUP BY runs in the scan; the outer aggregate runs in PostgreSQL
example: SELECT category, avg(avg_price) FROM (SELECT o.id, i.category, avg(i.price) avg_price FROM orders o, jsonb_to_recordset(o.items) i(category text, price float8) GROUP BY 1, 2) x GROUP BY 1
notes: One group per (order, key): fast, but the outer sort and aggregate stay.
query: @s2_per_order_union

query/feature: Per-order aggregates with the outer aggregate in the same scan: UNION ALL arms (up to 4), HAVING or WHERE on the inner aggregates, gates, ROLLUP / GROUPING SETS, count(DISTINCT id)
example: SELECT category, kind, avg(avg_price), count(DISTINCT order_id) FROM (... GROUP BY order_id, ...) x GROUP BY ROLLUP (category, kind)
notes: The scan keeps each order's inner aggregates and adds them to the outer groups: no group per order.
query: @s2_per_order_union

query/feature: Per-order aggregates whose arms group by more keys than the outer query, and count(DISTINCT id) with no outer key
example: SELECT cc, count(DISTINCT order_id), sum(units) FROM (... GROUP BY order_id, cc, category UNION ALL ... GROUP BY order_id, cc) x GROUP BY cc
query: -- key: -\nWITH base AS (SELECT o.id AS order_id, o.country_code AS cc, i.category AS mc, i.qty FROM orders o CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_to_recordset(o.items) AS i(category text, kind text, qty int, price float8, discount float8) WHERE o.store_id < 120 AND o.deleted_at IS NULL) SELECT cc, count(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders, count(*) AS cells, sum(units) AS units FROM (SELECT order_id, cc, mc AS category, sum(qty) AS units FROM base GROUP BY order_id, cc, mc UNION ALL SELECT order_id, cc, NULL::text, sum(qty) FROM base GROUP BY order_id, cc) x GROUP BY cc ORDER BY cc NULLS FIRST

query/feature: Per-order form with a volatile or mixed outer qual, a qual across arms, or more cell keys than the scan has
condition: the qual is per outer group and cell, not per row
example: WHERE avg_price > 100 OR kind = 'x'
notes: The inner arms may still run in the scan.
query: @t_two_level_where_volatile

query/feature: Key of a join as an expression of leaves (small.k = lower(o.source)) or ON conditions that are not keys
example: SELECT m.mapped_category, count(*) FROM orders o JOIN categories_map m ON m.category = lower(o.source) GROUP BY 1
query: @j_key_expr

query/feature: Lookup join with a volatile key or filter, a nondeterministic collation, more than 4 tables or 8 combos
condition: the combo cache evaluates once per distinct tuple, PostgreSQL per row
example: ON small.k = lower(o.source) AND random() < 0.5
query: @t_key_expr_volatile

query/feature: Two unnests in one query (jsonb_array_elements of two arrays), jsonb_array_elements_text and other set-returning functions
condition: one lateral unnest of an indexed array or object per query
example: FROM orders o, jsonb_array_elements(o.items) a, jsonb_array_elements(o.notes) n
query: SELECT o.status, count(*) FROM orders o, jsonb_array_elements(o.items) a, jsonb_array_elements(o.notes) n GROUP BY 1

query/feature: Partitioned tables, inheritance parents
condition: the index is per partition; the planner takes one table, no inheritance
example: SELECT status, count(*) FROM orders_part GROUP BY status
notes: Each partition can carry its own index; a query on the parent keeps the normal plan.
query: SELECT status, count(*) FROM orders_part GROUP BY status

query/feature: Row-level security that applies to the role
condition: the scan does not apply policies
example: SELECT grp, count(*) FROM cv_rls GROUP BY grp
notes: Superusers and table owners bypass RLS and keep the scan.
query: -- guc: role = sift_cov_user\nSELECT grp, count(*) FROM cv_rls GROUP BY grp

query/feature: HAVING
example: SELECT store_id, count(*) FROM orders GROUP BY store_id HAVING count(*) > 3
notes: HAVING, projection, ORDER BY and LIMIT stay in the plan above the scan.
query: @f_having

query/feature: ORDER BY and LIMIT of an aggregated result (top-N groups)
example: SELECT store_id, count(*) c FROM orders GROUP BY store_id ORDER BY c DESC LIMIT 3
notes: The aggregate is the scan; the sort and the limit are PostgreSQL's.
query: SELECT store_id, count(*) c FROM orders GROUP BY store_id ORDER BY c DESC, store_id LIMIT 3

query/feature: Window function over an aggregated subquery
example: SELECT status, c, rank() OVER (ORDER BY c DESC) FROM (SELECT status, count(*) c FROM orders GROUP BY status) x
query: SELECT status, c, rank() OVER (ORDER BY c DESC) FROM (SELECT status, count(*) c FROM orders GROUP BY status) x

query/feature: Window function in the same query level as the aggregate: rank() OVER (ORDER BY count(*))
condition: the aggregating query has no window functions
example: SELECT status, rank() OVER (ORDER BY count(*) DESC) FROM orders GROUP BY status
notes: Put the aggregate in a subquery.
query: SELECT status, count(*), rank() OVER (ORDER BY count(*) DESC) FROM orders GROUP BY status

query/feature: Window functions over rows, top-N rows (ORDER BY ... LIMIT with no aggregate), plain SELECT ... WHERE
condition: the column index serves aggregates only
example: SELECT id, total FROM orders ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 5
notes: Use a btree index for row queries.
query: SELECT id, total FROM orders ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 5

query/feature: FOR UPDATE, TABLESAMPLE on the indexed heap table, a set-returning function in the select list of the aggregate
condition: row locks, sampling and per-row expansion are not aggregates over the index
example: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE
query: @t_tablesample

query/feature: Parallel scan of the aggregate (count, sum, avg, min, max, count(DISTINCT), percentiles, keys of any kind, lookup joins, grouping sets)
example: SELECT store_id, count(*), sum(total) FROM orders GROUP BY store_id
notes: Workers are the ones a parallel sequential scan of the table would get (table size, parallel_workers, max_parallel_workers_per_gather) and are costed: a scan under about 15 ms keeps the leader alone. Not under a Gather: Workers Planned in the SiftAgg node. The merge of the workers' tables is costed per group: a query with hundreds of groups keeps the leader alone.
query:
-- guc: max_parallel_workers_per_gather = 2
-- guc: parallel_setup_cost = 0
-- guc: parallel_tuple_cost = 0
-- guc: min_parallel_table_scan_size = 0
SELECT source, count(*), sum(total) FROM orders GROUP BY source

query/feature: DISTINCT in the call, count(DISTINCT) of numeric expressions, ordered sets, lookup-joined aggregates, per-order arms
condition: run on the leader alone: no workers are planned
example: SELECT source, string_agg(DISTINCT status, ',') FROM orders GROUP BY source
notes: The scan is still the column scan; only the parallelism is missing.
query:
-- guc: max_parallel_workers_per_gather = 2
-- guc: parallel_setup_cost = 0
-- guc: parallel_tuple_cost = 0
-- guc: min_parallel_table_scan_size = 0
SELECT source, string_agg(DISTINCT status, ',') FROM orders GROUP BY source

query/feature: Float sums at any worker count
example: SELECT grp, sum(f8) FROM t GROUP BY grp
notes: 16 lanes added in lane order: the result is bit-identical for 0, 1, 2, ... workers and every SIMD level (not bit-identical to the heap-order sum of the normal plan).
query: SELECT coverage.workers_agree('SELECT grp, sum(f), avg(f), count(*) FROM cv_dml GROUP BY grp')

query/feature: Generic aggregates with a combine function: stddev and variance, corr, regr_*, bit_and, bit_or, bit_xor, sum(float4)
engine: SELECT source, stddev(total), bit_or(store_id) FROM orders GROUP BY source
example: SELECT source, stddev(total), bool_and(total > 10) FROM orders GROUP BY source
notes: Each worker keeps the partial states per group and the leader merges them by key value with the aggregate's combine function. The ordered, DISTINCT and joined-column kinds stay serial (X02). bool_and and bool_or are the exception (X05).
query:
-- guc: max_parallel_workers_per_gather = 2
-- guc: parallel_setup_cost = 0
-- guc: parallel_tuple_cost = 0
-- guc: min_parallel_table_scan_size = 0
SELECT source, stddev_samp(total), bit_or(store_id), regr_count(total::float8, store_id::float8) FROM orders GROUP BY source

query/feature: bool_and, bool_or, every in a parallel plan
condition: run on the leader alone: no workers are planned
example: SELECT source, bool_and(store_id > 3) FROM orders GROUP BY source
notes: They have a combine function, but the scan does not merge their states yet; the aggregate still runs in the column scan.
query:
-- guc: max_parallel_workers_per_gather = 2
-- guc: parallel_setup_cost = 0
-- guc: parallel_tuple_cost = 0
-- guc: min_parallel_table_scan_size = 0
SELECT source, bool_and(store_id > 3), bool_or(total > 400) FROM orders GROUP BY source

query/feature: Rows inserted after the index was built, not yet vacuumed (pages not all-visible)
example: SELECT grp, count(*), sum(v) FROM t GROUP BY grp
notes: Rows on pages the visibility map does not cover are checked in the heap under the query's snapshot, after the value filters.
query: SELECT grp, count(*), sum(v), avg(f) FROM cv_dml GROUP BY grp

query/feature: Updated and deleted rows, rolled-back inserts (dead versions before VACUUM)
example: SELECT tx, count(*) FROM t GROUP BY tx
notes: An UPDATE of an indexed column is a new tuple with its own index record.
query: SELECT tx, count(*), min(v), max(v) FROM cv_dml WHERE id % 25 <> 1 GROUP BY tx

query/feature: The transaction's own uncommitted changes
example: BEGIN; INSERT ...; SELECT count(*) ...;
notes: Compared with the normal plan in every state.
query: SELECT coverage.in_tx(ARRAY['INSERT INTO cv_dml SELECT 20000 + i, i % 5, i, i, ''n'' FROM generate_series(1, 100) i', 'UPDATE cv_dml SET v = v + 1 WHERE id % 7 = 0', 'DELETE FROM cv_dml WHERE id % 11 = 0'], 'SELECT grp, count(*), sum(v), min(v) FROM cv_dml GROUP BY grp') AND coverage.in_tx(ARRAY['INSERT INTO cv_tt SELECT * FROM cv_types WHERE id <= 40', 'UPDATE cv_tt SET i4 = i4 + 1 WHERE id % 9 = 0', 'DELETE FROM cv_tt WHERE id % 13 = 0'], 'SELECT grp, count(*), sum(i4) FROM cv_tt GROUP BY grp')

query/feature: Long snapshots, uncommitted writers, REPEATABLE READ and SERIALIZABLE
example: BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ; SELECT ...
notes: A SERIALIZABLE scan takes a relation predicate lock, so concurrent writers can cause 40001: retry.
query: SELECT coverage.snapshot('repeatable read', 'SELECT grp, count(*), sum(v) FROM cv_snap GROUP BY grp', ARRAY['INSERT INTO cv_snap SELECT 5000 + i, i % 5, i FROM generate_series(1, 200) i', 'UPDATE cv_snap SET v = v + 1 WHERE id % 7 = 0', 'DELETE FROM cv_snap WHERE id % 13 = 0']) AND coverage.snapshot('serializable', 'SELECT grp, count(*), sum(v) FROM cv_snap GROUP BY grp', ARRAY['INSERT INTO cv_snap SELECT 5000 + i, i % 5, i FROM generate_series(1, 200) i', 'UPDATE cv_snap SET v = v + 1 WHERE id % 7 = 0', 'DELETE FROM cv_snap WHERE id % 13 = 0'])

query/feature: VACUUM, REINDEX, promotion and merge of the segments, TID reuse
example: VACUUM orders; SELECT ...

query/feature: HOT updates of columns no index holds
example: UPDATE orders SET total = total + 1
query: -- pre: UPDATE cv_hot SET pad = pad || 'x' WHERE id % 2 = 0;\nSELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM heap_page_items(get_raw_page('cv_hot', 0)) WHERE (t_infomask2 & 16384) <> 0) AND coverage.same('SELECT grp, count(*), sum(v), max(id) FROM cv_hot GROUP BY grp')

query/feature: Hot standby (physical replica)
example: SELECT ... on the standby
notes: The index is generic WAL: a standby serves the scans read-only. A logical subscriber builds its own index (proof: script:replication).
query: SELECT grp, count(*), sum(v) FROM cv_dml GROUP BY grp

query/feature: All terms: body @@> 'clean wifi' (words are ANDed)
example: SELECT id FROM docs WHERE body @@> 'breakfast friendly'
notes: Case and accent folded; optional Snowball English stemming (stemmer = 'en').
query: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE memo @@> 'clean wifi'

query/feature: OR, parentheses, set of words {a b c}, boost ^n
example: SELECT id FROM docs WHERE body @@> '(pool OR spa) AND friendly^3'
query: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE memo @@> '((clean OR wifi) AND gift^3) OR {box label}'

query/feature: NOT (exclusion)
example: SELECT id FROM docs WHERE body @@> 'breakfast NOT noisy'
notes: A NOT needs a positive term in its AND group.
query: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE memo @@> 'clean NOT wifi'

query/feature: Phrase: "friendly staff"
example: SELECT id FROM docs WHERE body @@> '"friendly staff"'
notes: Decided from the word positions in the index (positions = on, the default); with positions = off, rechecked in the heap.
query: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE memo @@> '"gift invoice"'

query/feature: Prefix (cle*), wildcard (w?fi), regex (/thank.*/), fuzzy (clen~1)
example: SELECT id FROM docs WHERE body @@> 'brea* OR n?isy OR /no.*y/ OR frendly~1'
notes: Above sift.max_expansions (512) terms a leaf scores as one term. A regex has no back-references.
query: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE memo @@> 'cle* OR w?fi OR /thank.*/ OR clen~1'

query/feature: Field boost name:word, name:(a b), name:{a b}
condition: the index is built with the fields option
example: (name || chr(29) || admin1) @@> 'name:{gr* ho*}^3 OR (gr* ho*)'
notes: Without fields a colon is plain text. prefix_index = n makes short prefixes one lookup (autocomplete).
query: SELECT id FROM cv_places WHERE (name || chr(29) || admin1 || ' ' || country) @@> '(gr* ho*) AND (name:{gr* ho*}^3 OR (gr* ho*))' ORDER BY sift.score(ctid) DESC LIMIT 20

query/feature: Ranked top-k: ORDER BY sift.score(ctid) DESC LIMIT k
example: SELECT id, sift.score(ctid) FROM docs WHERE body @@> 'pool OR spa' ORDER BY sift.score(ctid) DESC LIMIT 10
notes: Exact BM25; skips blocks that cannot reach the top k; ties break by ctid. Also with a prepared LIMIT $1 and on materialized views.
query: SELECT id, sift.score(ctid) FROM orders WHERE memo @@> 'clean OR wifi' ORDER BY sift.score(ctid) DESC LIMIT 10

query/feature: count(*) of a match
example: SELECT count(*) FROM docs WHERE body @@> 'friendly'
notes: Counted from the index (SiftCount). With another filter in the WHERE, a SiftScan feeds PostgreSQL's count.
query: SELECT count(*) FROM orders WHERE memo @@> 'clean wifi'

query/feature: Match with other filters: score ranking plus a range or equality filter
example: SELECT id FROM docs WHERE body @@> 'friendly' AND published >= '2026-02-01' ORDER BY sift.score(ctid) DESC LIMIT 10
notes: With sift.filter_pushdown (on) the bitmap of the other quals (btree, BRIN, GIN) goes into the ranked scan, so a selective filter stays fast; results equal the post-filter plan. Prepared statements keep the filter as a child built only when it pays.
query: SELECT id, sift.score(ctid) FROM orders WHERE memo @@> 'clean OR wifi' AND placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' ORDER BY sift.score(ctid) DESC LIMIT 10

query/feature: Join with ranking
example: SELECT d.id, c.name FROM docs d JOIN categories c ON c.id = d.category WHERE d.body @@> 'friendly' ORDER BY sift.score(d.ctid) DESC LIMIT 10
notes: Nested loop; semi joins too.
query: SELECT o.id, s.kind FROM orders o JOIN stores s ON s.id = o.store_id WHERE o.memo @@> 'clean' ORDER BY sift.score(o.ctid) DESC LIMIT 10

query/feature: Several queries ORed: body @@> ANY (ARRAY['pool', 'spa'])
condition: a bitmap scan; no sift.score
example: SELECT id FROM docs WHERE body @@> ANY (ARRAY['pool', 'spa'])
notes: Write the OR in the query text to rank.
query: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE memo @@> ANY (ARRAY['clean', 'wifi'])

query/feature: Keyword facets: sift.facets(index, facet_index, query, limit)
condition: keyword analyzer, text keys, a table without row-level security
example: SELECT * FROM sift.facets('docs_body', 'docs_category', 'friendly OR pool', 10)
notes: Counts per value from the bitmaps, equal to the GROUP BY of the same snapshot; wins on broad queries over low-cardinality columns, GROUP BY wins on selective ones or thousands of values.
query: SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT value::text, count::bigint FROM sift.facets('orders_fts', 'orders_src_kw', 'clean OR wifi', 100) EXCEPT ALL SELECT source, count(*) FROM orders WHERE memo @@> 'clean OR wifi' GROUP BY source) x

query/feature: Partitioned tables: matching, count(*) and ranking through the parent
example: SELECT id FROM logs WHERE msg @@> 'disk "node 7"' ORDER BY sift.score(ctid) DESC LIMIT 3
notes: One index per leaf partition, global top-k by a MergeAppend. Scores are per partition statistics; sift.score() needs an index on every partition read.
query: SELECT id, sift.score(ctid) FROM cv_logs WHERE msg @@> 'disk "node 7"' ORDER BY sift.score(ctid) DESC LIMIT 3

query/feature: Several columns in one index
condition: concatenate them into one expression and query with the same expression
example: CREATE INDEX ON docs USING sift ((coalesce(title, '') || ' ' || coalesce(body, '')))
notes: A multicolumn index is refused (next rows).
query: SELECT id FROM cv_places WHERE (name || chr(29) || admin1 || ' ' || country) @@> 'gr*' ORDER BY sift.score(ctid) DESC LIMIT 5

query/feature: Match on a column with no sift index
condition: no index: the operator runs per row, with the same results
example: SELECT id FROM docs WHERE title @@> 'noisy'
query: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE country_code @@> 'US'

query/feature: A match ORed with a predicate on another column
condition: the index cannot answer the other branch
example: WHERE body @@> 'a' OR category = 1
query: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE memo @@> 'clean' OR store_id = 5

query/feature: BM25 index on a sift_table
example: SELECT count(*) FROM t WHERE tx @@> 'tx7'
notes: ambuild and scans run through the table access method.
query: SELECT count(*) FROM cv_tt WHERE tx @@> 'tx7'

query/feature: Parallel scan of a match (Gather over SiftScan / SiftCount)
condition: sift.parallel_scan = on (off by default); a ranked scan needs a LIMIT and one table; never with a pushed-down filter or over partitions
example: SET sift.parallel_scan = on
notes: A Gather costs milliseconds: it paid only for heavy residual quals on 218,058 articles (1.8x).
query:
-- guc: sift.parallel_scan = on
-- guc: max_parallel_workers_per_gather = 2
-- guc: parallel_setup_cost = 0
-- guc: parallel_tuple_cost = 0
-- guc: min_parallel_table_scan_size = 0
-- guc: min_parallel_index_scan_size = 0
SELECT id FROM orders WHERE memo @@> 'clean' AND length(memo) > 3

query/feature: Hot standby, replication, VACUUM, REINDEX CONCURRENTLY, pg_dump
notes: MVCC, generic WAL, partial and expression indexes. Logical replication carries rows, not indexes: create the index on the subscriber.
query: -- pre: VACUUM orders;\n-- pre: REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY orders_fts;\nSELECT pg_get_indexdef('orders_fts'::regclass) LIKE '%USING sift (memo)%' AND coverage.plan_of('SELECT count(*) FROM orders WHERE memo @@> ''clean''') ~ 'Custom Scan \(Sift(Scan|Count)\)'

query/feature: Aggregate over the rows of a match: GROUP BY with @@> in the WHERE
condition: the match runs on the BM25 index (SiftScan), the aggregate on the normal plan
example: SELECT source, count(*) FROM orders WHERE memo @@> 'clean' GROUP BY source
notes: SiftAgg does not take the @@> mask. For counts per value of a keyword column, sift.facets.
query: SELECT source, count(*) AS n, count(DISTINCT store_id) AS stores, min(placed_at) FROM orders WHERE memo @@> 'clean wifi' AND deleted_at IS NULL GROUP BY source ORDER BY source

query/feature: Aggregate over a ranked top-k (subquery with LIMIT) or a column aggregate joined to a ranked scan
condition: the sub-select is a plan, not a table the scan can read
example: SELECT status, count(*) FROM orders WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM orders WHERE memo @@> 'clean' ORDER BY sift.score(ctid) DESC LIMIT 100) GROUP BY 1
notes: The ranked scan stays on SiftScan; the aggregate on the normal plan.
query: SELECT status, count(*) FROM orders WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM orders WHERE memo @@> 'clean' ORDER BY sift.score(ctid) DESC LIMIT 100) GROUP BY 1

query/feature: sift.score() in WHERE
condition: 0A000; filter on the score from a subquery
example: SELECT ... WHERE body @@> 'a' AND sift.score(ctid) > 1
notes: sift.score() is computed by the scan: use it in the select list or ORDER BY of the query level that scans the table.
query: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE memo @@> 'clean' AND sift.score(ctid) > 1

query/feature: sift.score() with body @@> ANY (array), in UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE, FOR UPDATE, or a column with no sift index
condition: 0A000; write the OR in the query text, rank in a SELECT and change the rows by key
example: UPDATE t SET ... WHERE sift.score(ctid) > 0
query: SELECT id, sift.score(ctid) FROM orders WHERE memo @@> ANY (ARRAY['clean','wifi']) ORDER BY sift.score(ctid) DESC LIMIT 3

query/feature: NOT with no positive term: body @@> 'NOT wifi'
condition: 42601; add a positive term
example: SELECT id FROM docs WHERE body @@> 'NOT noisy'
notes: Also: queries over 256 leaves, nesting depth 32, phrases over 128 tokens, boosts over 10000.
query: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE memo @@> 'NOT wifi'

query/feature: BM25 index on several columns, a unique index, INCLUDE columns, a non-text key
condition: 0A000 (42704 for a non-text key); concatenate columns into one expression, cast the key to text
example: CREATE INDEX ON docs USING sift (title, body)
notes: One key per index; no plain, index-only or ordered scans.
query: CREATE INDEX cv_x ON orders USING sift (memo, status)

query/feature: sift_col: unique, INCLUDE
example: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ON t USING sift_col (id)
query: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX cv_x ON cv_types USING sift_col (i4)

query/feature: Aggregates over a sift_table: count, sum, avg, min, max, distinct, filters, grouping
example: SELECT grp, count(*), sum(i4) FROM t WHERE i4 > 100 GROUP BY grp
notes: The same SiftAgg node reads the column groups, the write segment (as in-memory batches) and the tombstones with the table's own visibility; no index is needed.
query: SELECT grp, count(*), sum(i4), min(d) FROM cv_tt WHERE i4 > 100 GROUP BY grp

query/feature: Backward scan: a SCROLL cursor fetching backward, FETCH PRIOR / LAST
example: DECLARE c SCROLL CURSOR FOR SELECT * FROM t; FETCH LAST FROM c; FETCH PRIOR FROM c
notes: Both directions, as a heap: the first backward step lists the units of the range and walks them from the last; no unit is decoded twice per step.
query: SELECT coverage.scroll_back('cv_tt')

query/feature: More than 127 columns
condition: 54000 at CREATE TABLE; at most 127 columns
example: CREATE TABLE t (c1 int, ..., c128 int) USING sift_table
notes: ADD COLUMN past 127 succeeds and the next write fails until a column is dropped.
query: DO $d$ BEGIN EXECUTE 'CREATE TEMP TABLE cv_w128 (' || (SELECT string_agg('c' || g || ' int', ',') FROM generate_series(1, 128) g) || ') USING sift_table'; END $d$

query/feature: TID range scans (ctid >= ... AND ctid < ...)
example: SELECT count(*) FROM t WHERE ctid >= '(0,1)' AND ctid < '(100,1)'
notes: A plain row scan: the aggregate scan does not take a ctid qual.
query: SELECT count(*) FROM cv_tt WHERE ctid >= '(0,1)' AND ctid < '(100,1)'

query/feature: TABLESAMPLE SYSTEM and BERNOULLI
example: SELECT count(*) FROM t TABLESAMPLE BERNOULLI (10) REPEATABLE (7)
notes: A heap table with a column index keeps the normal plan for TABLESAMPLE (No in the aggregate rows).
query: SELECT count(*) > 0 FROM cv_tt TABLESAMPLE BERNOULLI (50)

query/feature: COPY in and out, INSERT ... SELECT, CREATE TABLE AS, ALTER TABLE ... SET ACCESS METHOD
example: COPY t FROM STDIN
notes: Rows go through the write segment one at a time (no bulk column path).

query/feature: Row scans of some columns (SELECT a FROM t WHERE ...), btree, GIN, BRIN, BM25 indexes, bitmap scans
example: SELECT i4 FROM t WHERE i4 < 10
notes: Works as for a heap; a table access method is not told which columns a query needs, so every row scan decodes whole units. Only the aggregate scan reads just its columns.
query: SELECT i4 FROM cv_tt WHERE i4 < 10

query/feature: UPDATE, DELETE, ON CONFLICT, row locks, triggers, savepoints, VACUUM FULL, CLUSTER
condition: no HOT; shared row locks degrade to exclusive
example: UPDATE t SET ... WHERE ...
notes: An UPDATE writes a new version and a tombstone, both visible to the aggregate scan under MVCC.

query/feature: System columns xmin, xmax, cmin, cmax
condition: ctid and tableoid are the row's; xmin, xmax and cmin return placeholder values, not the row's transaction ids
example: SELECT xmin FROM t
notes: docs/COL-TAM.md and USAGE.md say 0A000 for these; the query runs.
query: SELECT xmin::text IS NOT NULL FROM cv_tt LIMIT 1

query/feature: Publishing a sift_table under wal_level = logical without pg_sift in shared_preload_libraries
condition: 0A000 on the first DML; preload pg_sift on the publisher and its standbys, or publish a heap staging table
example: CREATE PUBLICATION p FOR TABLE t
notes: A subscriber needs nothing. Unpublished tables never need the preload.
query: INSERT INTO cv_pub VALUES (1, 1)
